props.title: Only You

sections.content: Only You epitomizes the romantic destiny-driven comedies of the 1990s, following Marisa Tomei's Faith, who chases across Italy pursuing a man whose name matches her supposed soulmate. The film deliberately echoes Roman Holiday (1953) and Three Coins in the Fountain (1954) in its sweeping Italian locations and belief in fateful romance. Director Norman Jewison, who also helmed Moonstruck (1987), brings his trademark touch for combining romantic whimsy with grounded characters.

sections.content: The film sits perfectly within the 90s romantic globetrotting subgenre, alongside French Kiss (1995) and While You Were Sleeping (1995). These films share an optimistic view of love and destiny, often featuring women who break from their planned lives to pursue romance. Only You particularly shines in its use of Italian locations - from Venice to Rome to the Amalfi Coast - making the setting as much a character as the leads.

The chemistry between Marisa Tomei and Robert Downey Jr. drives the film, showcasing both actors' rom-com capabilities years before Downey would become Iron Man. Their dynamic recalls classic pairs like Katharine Hepburn and Cary Grant in Bringing Up Baby (1938), where initial friction evolves into undeniable attraction. The film's exploration of destiny versus choice echoes through later works like Serendipity (2001). SUBHEAD: The Italian Romance Revival

sections.content: Only You helped spark a revival of Italian-set romance films that continued with Much Ado About Nothing (1993) and later Life Is Beautiful (1997). This trend persisted into the 2000s with films like Under the Tuscan Sun (2003) and Letters to Juliet (2010), all sharing the notion that Italy itself possesses magical romantic properties that can transform lives and hearts.
